questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.**

Glad
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option (3) i.e. Gloomy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Glad"** means feeling pleasure, joy, or happiness. (खुश)

 
 
• **Example:** She was glad to hear the good news about her promotion.
 
 
 
• **"Gloomy"** refers to feeling downcast, sad, or depressed. (उदास)
 
 
• **Example:** The gloomy weather made everyone feel lethargic and unmotivated.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'glad'** is **'gloomy'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option (3) i.e. Gloomy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Cheery** (प्रसन्न): Full of cheerfulness and happiness.

 
 
• **Example:** Her cheery smile brightened everyone’s day.
 
 
 
• **Delighted** (प्रसन्नचित्त): Feeling or showing great pleasure.
 
 
• **Example:** They were delighted to meet their childhood friend after so many years.
 
 
 
• **Joyous** (आनंदमय): Feeling or causing great happiness and joy.
 
 
• **Example:** It was a joyous occasion as they celebrated their anniversary.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. 

It were so painful / to give up / my last hope.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **It were so painful**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is incorrect because the **subject-verb agreement** is incorrect.
 
• "It" is a **singular subject**, but "were" is a **plural verb**. The correct verb to use with a singular subject is "was."

Therefore, the correct sentence would be:*** It was__ so painful to give up my last hope.***

• **Improve: **make or become better.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Please sit down and have breakfast _______ us.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **with**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "'With' is the correct preposition used in this sentence because it indicates the relationship between the subject 'you' and the object 'us'. In this context, 'with' is used to show that the person being addressed is going to join the group of people who are already having breakfast. 
 
• 'With' is a preposition that is used to indicate association or accompaniment. It is used to show that two or more things or people are together or in the same place. In this sentence, 'with' is used to show that the person being addressed is going to be in the same place as the group of people who are already having breakfast. 
 
• In summary, 'with' is the correct preposition used in this sentence because it indicates the association and accompaniment of the person being addressed with the group of people who are already having breakfast."

Therefore, the correct sentence is:* Please sit down and have breakfast **with__** us.*

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’.

Both of __mine child passed__ the examination successfully.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **my children passed**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Option 1 is correct because it uses the plural form of ""child"" which is ""children"" to agree with the plural verb ""passed"". This makes the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Option 2 is incorrect because it uses the wrong verb (passes). "children" is a plural noun and hence, the verb that must agree with it must also be plural. "passes" is a singular verb and hence, it is incorrect.
 
• Option 3 is also incorrect because ""mine"" is a possessive pronoun that is used before a noun to show ownership. However, in this sentence, ""mine"" is used as a possessive pronoun before ""child,"" which is incorrect. The correct possessive pronoun to use before ""child"" is ""my."" Additionally, since there are two children, the plural form ""children"" should be used instead of ""child.""
 
• Option 4 is incorrect because it uses the singular form of ""child"" with the present tense verb ""pass"". This creates a subject-verb agreement error as the verb should be in the past tense to match ""passed"". Additionally, using the singular form of ""child"" is incorrect as the sentence is referring to multiple children.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **my children passed**.
